name: tx_fprem
coverage: FPREM + FPREM1 differential vs the pinned QEMU golden: complete reduction, |a|<|b| (Q=0), signed operands, fractional operands, large exponent ratios, the C2=1 partial path (single-shot AND the re-execution idiom: re-run until C2 clears, both ops), quotient condition codes (FPREM q=0..7 -> every C0/C3/C1 combination; FPREM1 nearest-quotient Q=0..7), zero/-0/NaN/+Inf operands (masked #IA -> QNaN indefinite, IE), all four control-word rounding modes (the remainder is exact, so RC is unobservable -- proven by running both ops under RC=nearest/down/up/tozero), and back-to-back engine users (FPREM;FPREM and FPREM1;FPREM1 with no reload, FPREM->FDIV, FDIV->FPREM, FPREM1->FSQRT -- the iterative configs share one unified divide/sqrt/remainder engine). The partial loops use an exponent ratio (~2^67) chosen so each engine pass stays well under the TB idle threshold.
x87_fprem1_cc_oracle_gap: The pinned QEMU's helper_fprem1 (fpu_helper.c helper_fprem_common(mod=false)) reaches floatx80_modrem with the quotient out-pointer NULL, so an FPREM1 retirement ALWAYS reports C0=C3=C1=0 in the golden. The RTL reports the architectural Q2/Q1/Q0 of the round-nearest quotient (SDM FPREM1). These ranges are the measured set of records whose fstat differs ONLY in C0/C3/C1 (mask 0x4300): each FPREM1 retire record plus the following records until the next CC-writing instruction. C2 (partial) and every exception bit compare at full strength everywhere. Regenerate the ranges when tx_fprem.s changes (the set is n-indexed).
